# Welcome to AIEI — AI Engineering Intelligence Index

AIEI answers one question: **Is your AI investment actually working?**

Most organizations measure AI adoption with activity metrics ("40% of code is AI-generated") or perception surveys ("developers feel more productive"). Neither tells you whether AI is producing better outcomes.

AIEI measures **four outcome dimensions**:

- **Q (Quality)** — Is AI-generated code better or worse than human code?
    
- **L (Lead Time)** — Is AI making your team ship faster at the system level?
    
- **R (Reliability)** — Are AI-assisted services stable in production?
    
- **C (Cost Efficiency)** — Does the ROI justify the investment?
    

These combine into a single **0–1 composite score** with configurable weight profiles.

## How to use this guide

Run each request in order (1→5). Each one builds on the previous.  
By the end, you'll have a working AIEI score and know exactly where to go next.

## Prerequisites

- Start the mock server: `node postman/mocks/aiei-mock-server.js`
    
- Or use the Postman local mock server (AIEI Mock Data Server collection)
    

### **AI and API landscape**

- **40% agentic AI cancellation projection: Gartner via Kong Inc. (2026)**
    
- **Multi-model fragmentation, xAI migration costs: JuheAPI (2026)**
    
- **API management market growth: Research and Markets (2026)**

- **2025 State of the API Report: 5,700+ respondents. postman.com/state-of-api**

- **Entire.io for AI provenance: entire.io (2026)**
    
- **Channel partnerships evolving: TSIA (2026)**

**Why start here?** R-Score can be computed from data Postman already has:
- SLO attainment from Postman Monitors
- Contract catch rate from Postman CLI/CI
- The other signals come from your observability stack

After this step, you'll have your first defensible AI effectiveness metric.

item.description:
# AIEI Setup Wizard

## The Story

Before you measure anything, you need to know the instruments work. This collection is the pre-flight checklist for the entire AIEI framework. It walks you through five sequential steps that configure your environment, validate connectivity, and confirm that every downstream collection has what it needs to run.

Think of it like preflight checks on an aircraft. No pilot skips them, no matter how many times they've flown the route. The AIEI Setup Wizard exists because misconfigured environments are the number one cause of false negatives in measurement pipelines — and a false negative in an AI effectiveness score can derail an entire engineering strategy.

## The Five Steps

### Step 1 — Set Mock Base URL

Writes the `mock_base_url` variable into your active environment. Every other collection reads from this variable, so if this step fails, nothing downstream will work.

### Step 2 — Validate Environment

Reads back the variable you just set and confirms it resolved correctly. Catches copy-paste errors, encoding issues, and environment-selection mistakes.

### Step 3 — Health Check

Pings the mock server to confirm it's alive and responding. A 200 here means the infrastructure is ready; anything else means you need to check the mock server deployment.

### Step 4 — Verify Mock Data

Pulls a sample payload from the mock server and validates its structure. This ensures the mock isn't just alive but actually returning the shape of data the scoring collections expect.

### Step 5 — Configuration Summary

Aggregates the results of Steps 1–4 into a single pass/fail verdict. If everything is green, you're cleared to proceed to smoke tests and scoring.

## Prerequisites

- The **AIEI Configuration** environment must be active
    
- A mock server must be deployed (see [15 AIEI Mock Data Server](https://collection/20784047-6338821a-3085-4749-a2e1-f65b397f5000))
    

## What Comes Next

→ [02 AIEI Smoke Tests](https://collection/20784047-91ce4f76-3c4e-48d2-9fb6-fa2e605abd89) to verify connectivity  
→ [03 AIEI Measurement Contract](https://collection/20784047-0dd7e33b-c66e-4f25-84a2-6018375e36a9) to validate data prerequisites

item.description:
# AIEI Smoke Tests

## The Story

**Run this right after the Setup Wizard passes.** These are your canary tests — the simplest possible checks that confirm the AIEI mock infrastructure is alive and responding before you invest time in heavier measurement collections.

Smoke tests exist because distributed systems fail in boring ways. DNS doesn't resolve. Environment variables point to the wrong host. Mock servers restart and come back on a different port. The Smoke Tests collection catches these failures in seconds, before they cascade into confusing errors three collections downstream.

The philosophy is simple: if you can't reach the mock server with a basic GET, nothing else matters yet.

## The Two Checks

### 1. Health Check (Hardcoded URL)
Hits the mock server health endpoint using a hardcoded URL. This isolates infrastructure availability from environment configuration — if this fails, the server itself is down.

### 2. Health Check (Environment Variable)
Hits the same endpoint but resolves the URL from `{{mock_base_url}}` in your active environment. If Check 1 passes but Check 2 fails, your environment is misconfigured.

Together, these two checks triangulate the problem: **server down** vs. **bad config**.

## When to Run
- After completing the [01 AIEI Setup Wizard](collection/20784047-4b457cdf-dc2f-4de7-9897-9391ab615c9f)
- After any infrastructure change (mock server redeployment, environment switch)
- As the first step in any CI/CD pipeline that includes AIEI scoring
- Whenever downstream collections return unexpected errors

## What Comes Next
→ [03 AIEI Measurement Contract](collection/20784047-0dd7e33b-c66e-4f25-84a2-6018375e36a9) to validate data prerequisites before scoring
→ [04 AIEI R-Score](collection/20784047-92a6734d-2913-4884-914f-8f608b94a209) to begin computing reliability scores

item.description:
# AIEI Connector Registry

The integration layer for the AI Effectiveness Index. This collection serves as the **connector registry** — mapping which official MCP servers and Postman API Network collections feed each AIEI scoring dimension.

> **Architecture principle:** AIEI does NOT ship custom MCP servers for third-party tools. We reference official, vendor-maintained MCP servers and API collections. The only custom MCP is the **AIEI Pipeline Runner** — the orchestration layer unique to this tool.

---

## Official MCP Servers (AI Agent Path)

These are vendor-maintained MCP servers. Connect them in Postman's MCP settings to enable AI agent access to AIEI signals.

| Provider | MCP Source | Feeds | Setup |
|----------|-----------|-------|-------|
| **GitHub** | `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp` | Q, L, R scores | GitHub PAT in Authorization header |
| **SonarQube** | [docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-mcp-server](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-mcp-server) | Q-Score | SonarQube token |
| **DX** | [github.com/get-dx/dx-mcp-server](https://github.com/get-dx/dx-mcp-server) | L-Score | DX API key ([docs.getdx.com/webapi](https://docs.getdx.com/webapi/overview/)) |
| **Vercel** | [vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp) | L, R scores | Vercel access token |
| **PagerDuty** | Postman Official MCP Server List | R-Score | PagerDuty API token |
| **Slack** | Postman Official MCP Server List (npm + docker) | Reporting | Slack bot token |
| **Supabase** | [github.com/supabase-community/supabase-mcp](https://github.com/supabase-community/supabase-mcp) | R, Q, C scores | Supabase access token + project ref |

## Official API Collections (Human/Runner Path)

For providers without MCP servers, use these validated Postman API Network collections via `pm.sendRequest()` in score collection pre-request scripts.

| Provider | Postman Network Forks | Feeds | Note |
|----------|----------------------|-------|------|
| **Datadog** | 16,584 | R-Score (CFR, uptime) | No MCP yet — use collection |
| **Linear** | 7 | L-Score (cycle times) | No MCP yet — use collection |
| **OpenAI** | 26,975 | C-Score (token spend) | Roadmap |

## Custom AIEI MCP (This Collection)

| Server | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| **AIEI Pipeline Runner** | Orchestrates scoring pipeline — discovers collections, triggers monitor runs, reports connector status |

## Pending / Roadmap

| Provider | Status | Feeds |
|----------|--------|-------|
| **Entire.io** | CLI exists ([github.com/entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli)), REST API not yet documented | All scores (AI provenance) |

---

## Why This Architecture

1. **Zero fabrication** — Every connector references a verified, documented source
2. **Vendor-maintained** — Official MCP servers and collections stay current without our intervention
3. **Postman-native** — Showcases how the Postman API Network and MCP ecosystem are designed to work together
4. **Plug-and-play** — Customers connect the official servers they have; mock data fills gaps
5. **The AIEI pipeline is the differentiator** — not the connectors. The connectors are the enhancing layer.
